footer.data: Klar is itself an AI system, and tells you so on every screen. Your descriptions stay in your own anonymous session and are deleted after 30 days without activity. Models are reached through OpenRouter; embeddings run on Nebius (region to be confirmed). Full list of providers in the privacy notice.

method.lead: Accuracy is something we test and publish, not something we promise. This page explains the test set, what we count, and where the method has limits.

set.title: The test set
set.text: The main test set is built from the Commission’s own worked examples of high-risk and not-high-risk systems, plus <ph>[N]</ph> cases written for Klar. Half of the Commission examples are removed from everything Klar can search, so it can’t simply look the answers up. Each case is labelled with its correct class and role by <ph>[WHO LABELS THE CASES]</ph>.

count.title: What we count
count.riskClass: Share of cases where Klar’s class matches the label: prohibited, high-risk, limited, minimal or out of scope.
count.falseLow: Share of prohibited or high-risk cases that Klar labelled lower. This is the costliest error, so we report it on its own.
count.citations: Share of cited provisions that exist in the legal text and say what Klar claims. Checked automatically against the consolidated Act.
count.checker: The same {{cases}} cases run through {{name}}, scored the same way.
count.checkerPending: The same <ph>[N]</ph> cases run through <ph>[CHECKER NAME]</ph>, scored the same way.

score.title: How a case is scored
score.runText: Every case goes through the full engine, in the Act’s order, with the same settings users get.
score.compareText: The class, role and deciding provision are compared with the label.
score.citationsText: Every cited provision is looked up in the legal text, by number.
score.uncertaintyText: A “needs more information” or “legally ambiguous” result counts as correct only if the label agrees the case is open.

limits.title: Limits
limits.sizeText: The test set has <ph>[N]</ph> cases. Small differences between runs are not meaningful.
limits.labelsText: Labels reflect <ph>[WHO LABELS THE CASES]</ph>’s reading of the Act and may be disputed.
limits.guidanceText: Some Commission guidance is still in draft; results may shift when it’s final.
limits.descriptionsText: Real users describe tools less completely than test cases do. Klar is only as accurate as the description it gets.
limits.penaltiesText: Klar covers the Act’s own maximum fines (Art. 99). National penalty rules, which each Member State lays down, are out of scope.

privacy.lead: How Klar handles what you type. Short version: your data stays in an anonymous session, is never used to train models, and is deleted after 30 days without activity.
privacy.template: This is a template. Every bracketed field must be completed, and the notice reviewed by a data protection adviser, before launch.

purposes.title: What Klar processes, and why
purposes.descriptionsText: To classify your tools and draft your documents, the service you ask for. Legal basis: <ph>[TO CONFIRM, E.G. ART. 6(1)(B) GDPR]</ph>.
purposes.questionsText: To answer them, with citations. Same basis.
purposes.logsText: To keep the service secure and working, kept for <ph>[LOG RETENTION]</ph>. Legal basis: <ph>[TO CONFIRM, E.G. ART. 6(1)(F) GDPR]</ph>.
purposes.neverText: Train models on your data, create profiles, or set tracking cookies.

kept.retentionText: All of this is deleted after 30 days without activity. In the app, Your data deletes it all at once, whenever you like.

processors.title: Who else processes it

rights.title: Your rights
rights.text: You can ask for access to your data, correction, deletion, restriction, a portable copy, or object to processing (Articles 15 to 21 GDPR). In the app, Your data lets you download or delete everything at once. You can also complain to a supervisory authority; for a company based in North Rhine-Westphalia that is the LDI NRW, the state data protection commissioner <ph>[CONFIRM]</ph>.

welcome.title: Let's see where your AI tools stand.

profile.establishedHint: Established outside the EU? The Act still applies when your tools' output is used in the EU (Art. 2(1)(c)), and a provider of high-risk systems appoints a representative in the EU (Art. 22).
profile.usedInHint: The Act applies to AI used in the EU, wherever the provider sits (Art. 2).

label.none: Neither an SME nor a small mid-cap

body.sme: SMEs get lighter documentation duties, and the lower of the two maximum fines applies to them (Art. 99(6)), not the higher one of Art. 99(3).
body.smc: For a small mid-cap, the lower of the two maximum fines applies to fines under Art. 99(4) and (5) (Art. 99(6a)), but not to breaches of the Art. 5 bans (Art. 99(3)). Small mid-caps may use the simplified documentation too (Art. 11(1)).
body.none: Neither the relief for SMEs (Art. 99(6)) nor the one for small mid-caps (Art. 99(6a)) applies, so the higher of the two maximum fines applies (Art. 99(3) to (5)).
body.noneOriginal: The relief for SMEs (Art. 99(6)) doesn't apply, so the higher of the two maximum fines applies (Art. 99(3) to (5)). The original 2024 text has no small mid-cap rules.

size.maybeSme: Klar looks at turnover only. With a balance sheet total of up to €43 m you may still count as an SME.
size.maybeSmc: Klar looks at turnover only. With a balance sheet total of up to €129 m you may still count as a small mid-cap.

art99_3.quote: Non-compliance with the prohibition of the AI practices referred to in Article 5 shall be subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 35 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 7 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher.

art99_6.quote: In the case of SMEs, including start-ups, each fine referred to in this Article shall be up to the percentages or amount referred to in paragraphs 3, 4 and 5, whichever thereof is lower.

art2_1_c.quote: providers and deployers of AI systems that have their place of establishment or are located in a third country, where the output produced by the AI system is used in the Union;

art22_1.quote: Prior to making their high-risk AI systems available on the Union market, providers established in third countries shall, by written mandate, appoint an authorised representative which is established in the Union.

art99_6a.quote: In the case of SMCs, each fine referred to in paragraphs 4 and 5 shall be up to the percentages or amount referred therein, whichever is lower.

who.heading: Who processes it
who.modelsDetail: OpenRouter passes each request on; its own processing isn’t limited to the EU. The models run in EU regions on Microsoft Azure and Google Vertex AI.
who.modelsRefusal: If Microsoft Azure's content filter blocks a check or a question to Klar, that request (for a check: the description and the facts and answers taken from it; for a question: the question and the result it's about, if any) is sent once more to Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite on Google Vertex AI in the EU (zero data retention, no training), for each request the filter blocked. This happens only when the filter blocks it.
who.searchDetail: Nebius, reached through OpenRouter, turns your description into a search of the Act (embeddings). Nebius was chosen as an EU host, but OpenRouter gives this endpoint no region tag, so its region is <ph>[TO CONFIRM WITH NEBIUS]</ph>.
who.storageDetail: Your saved data, visible only to you.
who.noTraining: Every request to a model is sent with zero data retention and no training.

todo.heading: What you need to do

intro.provider: The tool is placed on the market or put into service under your name, so the duties for building, documenting and monitoring it are yours.
intro.deployer: You didn't build the tool, so most technical duties sit with its provider. As the company using it, you must use it as instructed, keep people in charge of it, and tell staff and the people it affects.
intro.importer: You bring the tool into the EU, so you check that its provider did its part before you sell it (Art. 23).
intro.distributor: You pass the tool on, so you check that it carries the required marking and documents before you do (Art. 24).

todo.minimal: No specific duties for this tool. One general duty applies to every company that uses AI:
todo.limited: Tell people they're dealing with AI. Klar drafts the disclosure for you.

hero.badge: Updated for the Digital Omnibus, in force since 27 July 2026
hero.title: Where does your AI tool stand under the AI Act?
hero.lead: Describe it in plain words, in English or German. Klar runs the Act's checks in their legal order, cites the provision behind every step, and turns the result into a to-do list with dates.
hero.note: Free, no account needed. Guidance, not legal advice.
hero.exampleLabel: An example: the Act's checks on one description
hero.description: We're a 40-person logistics company. We use a tool that reads incoming job applications, scores them, and shows HR a ranked shortlist. We bought it from a vendor and didn't change it.

scope.finding: An AI system used in the EU

prohibited.finding: No match with a banned practice

high_risk.name: High-risk
high_risk.quote: “…an AI system referred to in Annex III shall always be considered to be high-risk where the AI system performs profiling of natural persons.”

hero.role: You're the deployer. Duties apply from 2 December 2027.

dates.title: The dates moved in July 2026.
dates.lead: The Digital Omnibus, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, changed deadlines and added two prohibitions. Many sources online still show the old dates. Klar classifies under the amended text by default.

items.prohibitions: Two new prohibitions apply. The marking grace period ends for systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026.
items.annexIII: High-risk duties for systems listed in Annex III, such as recruitment or credit scoring.
items.annexI: High-risk duties for AI in products covered by EU product law (Annex I).

how.title: It checks in the Act's order, and shows its work.
how.lead: The order is fixed and no check is skipped. Inside each step, Klar fetches the provision by number where the law says where to look, and searches by meaning where it doesn't.

scope.name: Scope
scope.question: Is it an AI system in the legal sense, and does the Act apply where you use it?

prohibited.name: Prohibited practices
prohibited.question: Does it match a banned use? If it does, the checks stop here.

high_risk.name: High-risk
high_risk.question: Is it listed in Annex III, and does the Article 6(3) filter exempt it? Annex I products are flagged.

transparency.name: Transparency
transparency.question: Does it talk with people, or generate or change images, audio, video or text?

how.role: Then your role, and the duties that come with it: provider, deployer, importer or distributor, including the Article 25 switch.
how.evidenceLead: Every step says where its key fact came from, so you can challenge it.

evidence.assumed: a default we ask you to confirm

unsure.title: When it isn't sure, it says so.
unsure.lead: No confidence scores that nobody calibrated. A step can end in one of two honest outcomes instead of a guess.

info.summary: A fact that decides the outcome is missing. Klar names it and asks.
info.question: Does the shift planner use performance or behaviour data to assign work?
info.next: Your answer is added to the description and the checks run again.

ambiguous.summary: The facts are clear, but the law and guidance don't settle it. You see both readings.
